# Embedded skill: deck-build-standards

# deck-build-standards

Turns the content contract into checkable build rules and applies a consistent visual standard, so decks from different runs look like they came from the same organisation.

## WHEN TO USE

After Gate 2 (storyline approval — see the agent's AGENT.md), during and after the build. Gate 1 (audience + decision) also lives in AGENT.md, not here.

## LAYOUT STANDARDS

- Title slide: title, subtitle, date, author. Nothing else.
- Content slides: assertion headline in the top zone, body below, source footnote at the bottom.
- One chart per slide maximum. A slide with two charts is two slides or a table.
- Every visual element (chart, diagram, infographic) must be accompanied by supporting data or explanatory text on the same slide. No standalone visuals without context.
- Consistent left alignment. No centred body text.
- No more than two font sizes in the body.
- Sentence case in headlines, not title case, not all caps.

## CHART RULES

- Label axes and units on every chart.
- State the period covered in the chart title or subtitle.
- Never truncate a bar chart axis. Truncated axes exaggerate and will be spotted.
- Order categories by value unless there is a natural order such as time.
- Put the number on the bar when there are fewer than eight bars.
- One message per chart, stated in the chart title.

## SOURCE FOOTNOTE FORMAT

```
Source: <origin>, <specific location>, <date accessed or period>
```

Every slide with a number has one. No exceptions.

## PRE-DELIVERY CHECKLIST

Run all of these before returning the file. Report the result of each.

1. Does every slide headline assert something.
2. Does any headline contain "and" joining two ideas.
3. Does every number have a source footnote.
4. Are there any placeholder texts left in the deck.
5. Does the headline-only read give the full argument.
6. Is any slide over six bullets or over two lines per bullet.
7. Are all charts labelled with units and period.
8. Is the slide count justified by the argument.
9. Does any heading text collide with the subheading or content below it. Check every slide where the heading wraps to two lines. The subheading and content zone must shift down. A collision is a failed check.
10. Does any slide contain an infographic, diagram, or chart without accompanying data or explanatory text. A visual alone on a slide is a failed check. Every visual needs numbers, labels, or a written explanation alongside it.

Report the checklist result to the user alongside the file. A build that fails a check ships with the failure stated, not hidden.

## BRAND APPLICATION

Pull colours, fonts, logos, and decorative shape assets from the `brand-for-pptx` and `pptx-master` skills bound to this agent. These skills carry the full Sarvam brand spec: color tokens (Orange `#E6651B` / `#A5460F` / `#FEEDE6`, Blue `#3333CC` / `#E8EFFC`), fonts (Season Mix for headings, Matter for body), the Main Gradient for title/conclusion slides, the 60-slide template.pptx with embedded fonts, and 22 decorative shape assets with product mappings.

When building a deck:
- Use `pptx-master` as the primary build path: copy the template.pptx, delete unused layouts, swap content into the pre-built on-brand slides. Fonts are already embedded.
- Use `brand-for-pptx` for the brand spec (exact hex codes, font sizes, layout coordinates, logo variants, asset registry) and for its QA process.
- Apply the brand skill's mandatory enforcement: footer bar, monogram, and standard layout positions on every content slide.
- Never use a neutral palette. The Sarvam brand is the default. If both brand skills are present, always apply the brand.

## NEVER

- Never invent a chart from data you were not given.
- Never use a stock photo.
- Never build the deck before the storyline is approved.
